newsitem.title: USA: De Silguy - increasing number may be ready for EMU.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy - increasing number may be ready for EMU.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves- Thibault de Silguy said Sunday that an increasing number of European countries may be ready to meet criteria for a single European currency after a big effort to cut budget deficits.
"I think a significant number will be ready in 1997. When I see the present efforts I am optimistic," he told reporters at a meeting of the IMF and World Bank.
"Probably with more effort in the way of consolidation, I am sure there will be a significant number -- perhaps an increasing number," de Silguy said.

Italy and Spain last week unveiled budgets designed to bring their deficits to or below three percent of Gross Domestic Product next year, the crucial year for deciding which countries will join a single currency when it is launched in 1999.
"Italy has made a huge effort to meet the conditions to be able to switch to the Euro at the end of 1997," he said.
He said, however, there was no question of softening Maastricht Treaty standards for entry to monetary union.
De Silguy had said before the European government announced their cost-cutting budgets this September that around seven countries would be ready for monetary union.
